title: TrustChain-Review: A Risk-Adaptive Blockchain and Game-Theoretic Framework for Trustworthy AI-Assisted Code Review
content: AI-assisted software development is reshaping how code is generated, reviewed, tested, and maintained. However, the increasing use of AI coding assistants introduces new trust and quality-assurance challenges. Developers may submit AI-generated code without sufficient verification, reviewers may approve changes superficially, and platform-level reputation scores may be affected by biased, incomplete, or malicious feedback. Many existing code-review and reputation mechanisms remain centralized, weakly auditable, or insufficiently adaptive to strategic behaviour among developers, reviewers, and platform operators. To address these limitations, this paper proposes TrustChain-Review, a blockchain-enabled game-theoretic incentive framework for trustworthy AI-assisted code review. The framework integrates three complementary layers. First, a blockchain-based evidence layer is proposed to record or reference review activities, code-change metadata, review comments, dataset-observed quality-related evidence, and reputation updates in a tamper-resistant manner. The empirical part of this study uses dataset-observed fields from the Diff Quality Estimation dataset, while test outcomes, vulnerability reports, and post-merge defect signals are considered future deployment-level evidence. Second, a game-theoretic incentive layer models the strategic interactions among developers, reviewers, and the platform, capturing trade-offs between effort, reward, penalty, transparency cost, and reputation gain. Third, a risk-adaptive governance mechanism determines when the expected trust, auditability, and risk-reduction benefits of evidence-based review justify its additional operational cost. This decision rule connects contribution risk, developer effort, reviewer reliability, reputation effects, and platform governance cost within a unified game-theoretic framework. The proposed framework aims to improve the reliability of reputation scores, reduce the impact of low-quality or dishonest feedback, and encourage cooperative behaviour in AI-assisted software ecosystems. The framework is evaluated through a controlled simulation calibrated with empirical characteristics extracted from the Diff Quality Estimation dataset, including balanced review-need labels, patch-length statistics, review-comment availability, and language-metadata coverage. The results show that TrustChain-Review improves reputation accuracy, trust convergence, malicious review detection, and superficial review detection compared with simple reputation, centralized reputation, blockchain-only, and static-incentive baselines, while introducing a higher governance-cost trade-off. These findings suggest that evidence-based governance is most valuable when contribution risk and trust requirements are sufficiently high to justify its additional cost, while simpler governance may remain more appropriate for low-risk review settings.
